RI values of the retro-reflector lower than those shown in the last two columns of Table 3 are not permissible within the solid angle having the centre of reference as its apex and bounded by the planes intersecting along the following lines: (β1 = ±10°, β2 = 0°) (β1 = ±5°, β2 = ±20°).

In the case where a retro-reflector of Class IA or Class IB is intended to be installed with its H plane at a mounting height less than 750 mm above the ground, the RI values are verified only up to an angle of 5° downwards.
The testing of the colour for the retro-reflector (night-time colour) shall be carried out according to the method described in paragraph 4.2.1.
The trichromatic coordinates of the luminous flux reflected by the retro-reflector must be within the limits for the night-time colour red as specified in UN Regulation No. 48.

The conformity requirements for the retro-reflective device shall be considered satisfied from a mechanical and geometric standpoint, if the differences do not exceed inevitable manufacturing deviations within the requirements of this Regulation.

With respect to photometric performances, the conformity of mass-produced retro-reflective devices shall not be contested if, when testing photometric performances of any retro-reflective device chosen at random no measured value deviates unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from the minimum values prescribed in this Regulation.
The chromaticity coordinates of the retro-reflective device shall be complied with.

For each type of retro-reflective device the holder of the approval mark shall carry out at least the tests of conformity, at appropriate intervals, in accordance with the provisions of this Regulation.

If any sampling of the retro-reflective device shows non-conformity with regard to the type of test concerned, further samples shall be taken and tested, and the manufacturer shall take steps to ensure the conformity of the production concerned.
Tests of conformity of the retro-reflective device shall cover the photometric and colorimetric characteristics and the resistance to penetration of water.
Tests of conformity of the retro-reflective device shall generally be carried out in accordance with the methods set out in this Regulation.

In any test of conformity of the retro-reflective device carried out by the manufacturer, equivalent methods may be used with the consent of the Type Approval Authority, provided the manufacturer proves that the applied methods are equivalent to those laid down in this Regulation.
The test apparatus used for conformity tests of the retro-reflective device shall be regularly calibrated and correlated with measurements made by a Type Approval Authority.
Samples of retro-reflective devices shall be selected at random from the production of a uniform batch.
The sampled retro-reflective device shall be subjected to photometric measurements at the points and the chromaticity coordinates provided for in the Regulation.

The manufacturer shall carry out a statistical study of the test results of the retro-reflective device and define, in agreement with the Type Approval Authority, criteria governing the acceptability of his products in order to meet the specifications laid down in paragraph 3.5.1. of this Regulation, such that, with a confidence level of 95 per cent, the minimum probability of passing a spot check in accordance with Annex 3 (first sampling) would be 0.95.

The retro-reflective devices shall conform from a mechanical and a geometric standpoint, in accordance with the requirements of this Regulation, if any, with differences not exceeding inevitable manufacturing deviations.

When testing photometric performances of any retro-reflective device chosen at random, no measured value shall deviate unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from the minimum values prescribed in this Regulation, retro-reflective devices with apparent defects being disregarded.
The chromaticity coordinates of the retro-reflective devices shall be complied with.
The deviation of any specimen of samples A and B (all four retro-reflective devices) shall be not more than 20 per cent.

One of the retro-reflectors of sample A after the sampling procedure in paragraph 2. shall pass the test according to the procedure described in paragraph 1. of Part 2 of Annex 6; however, if the test on sample A is not complied with, the two retro-reflective devices of sample B shall be subjected to the same procedure, and both shall pass the test.
When the RI of a retro-reflective device is measured for an angle β of β1 = β2 = 0°, it shall be ascertained whether any mirror effect is produced by slightly turning the device.
If there is any mirror effect when the RI of the retro-reflective device is measured for an angle β of β1 = β2 = 0°, a reading shall be taken with an angle β of β1 = -5°, β2 = 0°.

With an illumination angle β of β1 = β2 = 0°, or the angle specified in paragraph 5. of this Regulation, and an angle of divergence of 20', retro-reflective devices which are not marked "TOP" shall be rotated about their axes of reference to the position of minimum RI, which must conform to the value specified in paragraph 5. of this Regulation.

When the RI of a retro-reflective device not marked "TOP" is measured for the other angles of illumination and divergence, the retro-reflective device shall be placed in the position corresponding to this value of ε, except that if the specified values are not attained, the device may be rotated about its axis of reference ±5° from that position.

With an illumination angle β of β1 = β2 = 0°, or the angle specified in paragraph 4. of this Regulation, and an angle of divergence of 20', retro-reflective devices marked "TOP" shall be rotated about their axes ±5°, and the RI must not fall below the prescribed value in any position assumed by the device during this rotation.
If for the direction β1 = β2 = 0°, and for ε = 0° the RI exceeds the specified value by 50 per cent or more, all measurements for all angles of illumination and divergence shall be made for ε = 0°.
The CIE-angular system as shown in Figure A4-I shall be used for specifying and measuring the retro-reflective device.

For testing the retro-reflection the retro-reflective devices shall be illuminated with a CIE Standard Illuminant A (ISO 11664-2:2007(E)/CIE S 014-2/E:2006) and measured as described in Part 1 of Annex 4.
The angular diameter of the source for the measurement of retro-reflective devices shall be δ≤10'.
The angular diameter of the measuring device for the measurement of retro-reflective devices shall be γ≤10'.
The angular diameter of the illuminated area for the measurement of retro-reflective devices shall be η≤80'.
The measuring distance shall be chosen in such an order that at least the limits for the angles δ, γ and η given above and illustrated in Figure A4-III are respected, but not lower than 10 m.

The illuminance over the useful area of the retro-reflective device, measured perpendicular to the incident light, shall be sufficiently uniform, and the variation in the value of the illuminance shall comply with the condition: max/min ≤ 1.05.
The photometer head shall be corrected to the spectral luminous efficiency for the CIE standard photometric observer in photopic vision.

The photometer head shall not show a perceptible change in local sensitivity within the area of its aperture; otherwise suitable provisions shall be added, e.g. the application of a diffusing window at a certain distance in front of the sensitive surface.
The field of view of the photometer head and the spread of light from both the sample and the source shall be restricted as much as possible.
Reflections from the floor and walls which occur over the relatively long test distances used shall be screened from both the sample and the photometer head by baffles.

The residual stray light value measured when the sample is covered by an opaque matt black surface, zigzag folded black paper of the same size and shape or a specular black surface suitably oriented with a light trap shall be subtracted from that measured on the retro-reflective device.

The shape of the illuminating surfaces of the retro-reflective device of Class IA or IB shall not be easily confused with the triangular shape, as prescribed for retro-reflectors mentioned in paragraph 2.1., from an observation distance of 10 metres.

In the case of moulded plastics reflectors of retro-reflecting devices of Classes IA or IB, the retro-reflective device shall be kept for 48 consecutive hours in a dry atmosphere at a temperature of 65 °C ± 2 °C, after which the sample shall be allowed to cool for 1 hour at 23 °C ± 2 °C.
After the resistance to heat test, no cracking or appreciable distortion of the retro-reflective device and, in particular, of its optical component must be visible.

The retro-reflector, whether part of a lamp or not, shall be stripped of all removable parts and immersed for 10 minutes in water at a temperature of 50 °C ± 5 °C, the highest point of the upper part of the illuminating surface being 20 mm below the surface of the water.

The water immersion test of the retro-reflector shall be repeated after turning the retro-reflective device through 180°, so that the illuminating surface is at the bottom and the rear face is covered by about 20 mm of water.
The retro-reflector sample units shall then be immediately immersed in the same conditions in water at a temperature of 25 °C ± 5 °C.

No water shall penetrate to the reflecting surface of the retro-reflecting optical unit of the retro-reflector; if visual inspection clearly reveals the presence of water, the device shall not be considered to have passed the test.

If visual inspection does not reveal the presence of water or in case of doubt, the RI of the retro-reflector shall be measured by the method described in paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. of this Regulation, the retro-reflective device being first lightly shaken to remove excess water from the outside.

As an alternative, at the request of the manufacturer, the moisture and dust tests of Annex 6 Part 3 shall be applied to the retro-reflective device of Class IB or IIIB to verify resistance to water penetration.

The water spray cabinet shall be equipped with a nozzle(s) which provides a solid cone water spray of sufficient angle to completely cover the sample device, and the centreline of the nozzle(s) shall be directed downward at an angle of 45° ± 5° to the vertical axis of a rotating test platform.
The rotating test platform of the water spray cabinet shall have a minimum diameter of 140 mm and rotate about a vertical axis in the centre of the cabinet.

The precipitation rate of the water spray at the device shall be 2.5 (+1.6/-0) mm/min as measured with a vertical cylindrical collector centred on the vertical axis of the rotating test platform, with a collector height of 100 mm and an inside diameter of a minimum of 140 mm.
A sample device mounted on a test fixture, with initial RI measured and recorded, shall be subjected to the water spray test.
During the water spray test all drain holes and other openings of the device shall remain open, and drain wicks, when used, shall be tested in the device.
During the water spray test the device shall be rotated about its vertical axis at a rate of 4.0 ± 0.5 min-1.

If the retro-reflector is reciprocally incorporated or grouped with signalling or lighting functions, these functions shall be operated at design voltage according to a cycle of 5 min ON (in flashing mode, where appropriate), 55 min OFF.
The water spray test shall last 12 hours (12 cycles of 5/55 min).
After the water spray test the rotation and the water spray shall be turned OFF and the device allowed to drain for 1 hour with the cabinet door closed.

Upon completion of the drain period, the interior of the device shall be observed for moisture accumulation and no standing pool of water shall be allowed to be formed, or which can be formed by tapping or tilting the device.
After the water spray test and drain period, the RI shall be measured according to the method specified in Part 1 of Annex 4 after having dried the exterior of the device with a dry cotton cloth.

The interior of the dust exposure test chamber shall be cubical in shape in size 0.9 to 1.5 m per side, with an internal chamber volume, not including a "hopper shaped" bottom, of 2 m3 maximum, charged with 3 to 5 kg of the test dust, and the chamber shall have the capability of agitating the test dust by means of compressed air or blower fans in such a way that the dust is diffused throughout the chamber.
The test dust used shall be fine powdered cement in accordance with standard ASTM C 150-84.
A sample device, mounted on a test fixture, with the initial RI measured and recorded, shall be exposed to dust.
During the dust exposure test all drain holes and other openings of the device shall remain open, and drain wicks, when used, shall be tested in the device.
The mounted device shall be placed in the dust chamber no closer than 150 mm from a wall, and devices with a length exceeding 600 mm shall be horizontally centred in the test chamber.

The test dust shall be agitated as completely as possible by compressed air or blower(s) at intervals of 15 min for a period of 2 to 15 s for the duration of 5 hours, and the dust shall be allowed to settle between the agitation periods.

Upon completion of the dust exposure test, the exterior of the device shall be cleaned and dried with a dry cotton cloth and the RI measured according to the method specified in paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. of this Regulation.
The retro-reflector shall be so designed that it retains the prescribed photometric and colorimetric characteristics despite the humidity and corrosive influences to which it is normally exposed.

The resistance of the front surface of the retro-reflector to tarnishing and of the protection of the rear face to deterioration shall be checked, particularly when an essential metal component seems liable to be attacked, with the testing of resistance to corrosion as described in ISO Standard 9227:2017.

The lamp, since the retro-reflective device is combined with a light, shall be stripped of all removable parts and subjected to the action of a saline mist for a period of 50 hours, comprising two periods of exposure of 24 hours each, separated by an interval of two hours during which the sample is allowed to dry.

In the case of retro-reflective devices with essential metal components susceptible to corrosion, the saline mist shall be produced by atomizing, at a temperature of 35 °C ± 2 °C, a saline solution obtained by dissolving 5 parts by weight of sodium chloride in 95 parts of distilled water containing not more than 0.02 per cent of impurities.
Immediately after completion of the corrosion test, the sample shall not show signs of excessive corrosion liable to impair the efficiency of the retro-reflective device.

The coefficient of retro-reflection RA of the retro-reflective areas, when measured after a recovery period of 48 hours as specified in Part 2 of Annex 6, at an entrance angle of β2 = 5° and an observation angle of α = 20', shall be not less than the value in Table 9 or more than the value in Table 10 respectively.
Before measuring the coefficient of retro-reflection after the corrosion test, the surface of the retro-reflector shall be cleaned to remove salt deposits from the saline mist.
The reverse side of the mirror-backed retro-reflective device of Class IA or IB with an accessible rear face shall be brushed with a hard nylon brush.

After having brushed, in the case of moulded plastics reflectors as Classes IA, IB, IIIA, IIIB and IVA, the rear face of the retro-reflective device, a cotton cloth soaked in the mixture defined in Part 1 of Annex 7 shall be applied to the said rear face for one minute, after which the cotton cloth is removed and the retro-reflective device left to dry.
As soon as evaporation is completed, the reverse side of the retro-reflective device shall be brushed with the same brush as before.

The RI of the retro-reflective device shall then be measured, according to paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. of this Regulation, after the whole surface of the mirror-backed rear face has been covered with Indian ink.
The accelerated artificial weathering apparatus used for testing the retro-reflector shall be in accordance with EN ISO 4892-1:2016 and EN ISO 4892-2:2013.
The accelerated artificial weathering apparatus shall be capable to control temperature and relative humidity and shall be equipped with a water spray system.
The water spray system of the accelerated artificial weathering apparatus shall be capable to spray a minimum of 0.3 ml/cm² within 5 minutes.
The spray water used in the accelerated artificial weathering test shall be in accordance to the requirements of EN ISO 4892-2:2013.
For temperature measurement in the accelerated artificial weathering test either a Black-Standard or a Black-Panel thermometer can be used (test method TM1 and TM2).
The retro-reflective device samples shall be exposed in accordance with EN ISO 4892-2:2013 using the parameters given in Table A6-1 for a period of 500 hours.

When test method TM1 (Black-standard thermometer) is used, the retro-reflective device samples shall be exposed according to cycle No. 1 of EN ISO 4892-2:2013 with 102 min dry at a broadband (300 to 400 nm) irradiance of 60 ± 2 W/m², a narrowband (340 nm) irradiance of 0.51 ± 0.02 W/m², a black-standard temperature of 65 ± 3 °C and a relative humidity of 50 ± 10 %, followed by 18 min water spray at a broadband irradiance of 60 ± 2 W/m² and a narrowband irradiance of 0.51 ± 0.02 W/m².

When test method TM2 (Black-panel thermometer) is used, the retro-reflective device samples shall be exposed according to cycle No. 4 of EN ISO 4892-2:2013 with 102 min dry at a broadband (300 to 400 nm) irradiance of 60 ± 2 W/m², a narrowband (340 nm) irradiance of 0.51 ± 0.02 W/m², a black-panel temperature of 63 ± 3 °C and a relative humidity of 50 ± 10 %, followed by 18 min water spray at a broadband irradiance of 60 ± 2 W/m² and a narrowband irradiance of 0.51 ± 0.02 W/m².
Preparation of test specimens of the retro-reflective device for the accelerated artificial weathering test shall be in accordance with the general guidelines given in EN ISO 4892-2:2013.

For the resistance to fuels test, the outer surface of the retro-reflective device and, in particular, of the illuminating surface, shall be lightly wiped with a cotton cloth soaked in a test mixture of 70 vol. per cent of n-heptane and 30 vol. per cent of toluol.

After about five minutes following the wiping with the test mixture, the outer surface of the retro-reflective device shall be inspected visually and must not show any apparent surface changes, except that slight surface cracks will not be objected to.

In the resistance to lubricating oils test for moulded plastics retro-reflectors of Classes IA, IB, IIIA, IIIB and IVA, the outer surface of the retro-reflective device and, in particular, the illuminating surface, shall be lightly wiped with a cotton cloth soaked in a detergent lubricating oil.

In the resistance to lubricating oils test for moulded plastics retro-reflectors of Classes IA, IB, IIIA, IIIB and IVA, after about 5 minutes the surface of the retro-reflective device shall be cleaned.

In the resistance to lubricating oils test for moulded plastics retro-reflectors of Classes IA, IB, IIIA, IIIB and IVA, the RI of the retro-reflective device shall then be measured according to paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. of this Regulation.
The approval marking arrangement shall be made in accordance with paragraph 3.3. of this Regulation; the arrangements in Annex 10 are given merely as examples.
The approval number of the retro-reflective device must be placed close to, but in any position in relation to, the circle surrounding the letter "E".
The digits constituting the approval number of the retro-reflective device must face the same way as the "E".
The group of symbols indicating the class of the retro-reflective device must be diametrically opposite the approval number.

The rear combination lamp (rear position, stop and reversing lamp functions and retro-reflector) shall be so fitted that under normal conditions of use as defined in paragraphs 2.3.10., 2.3.10.1. and 2.3.10.2. and notwithstanding any vibrations to which it may be subjected, it retains the characteristics prescribed by this Regulation and enables the vehicle to comply with the requirements of this Regulation.
It shall not be possible for the lamps of the rear combination lamp to be inadvertently maladjusted.

For the rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp and retro-reflector of the rear combination lamp, the reference axis of the lamp when fitted to the vehicle shall be parallel to the bearing plane of the vehicle on the road, with a tolerance of ±3°.

For the rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp and retro-reflector of the rear combination lamp, the reference axis of the lamp when fitted to the vehicle shall be parallel to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle, with a tolerance of ±3°.
Any specific instructions as regards fitting of the rear combination lamp laid down by the manufacturer shall be complied with.

In the absence of specific instructions, the height and orientation of the rear combination lamp (rear position, stop and reversing lamps and retro-reflector) shall be verified with the vehicle unladen and placed on a flat, horizontal surface, in the condition defined in paragraphs 2.3.10., 2.3.10.1. and 2.3.10.2.

In the absence of specific instructions, the lamps constituting a pair (rear position lamps, stop lamps, reversing lamps and rear retro-reflectors of the left- and right-hand rear combination lamps) shall be fitted to the vehicle symmetrically in relation to the median longitudinal plane (this estimate to be based on the exterior geometrical form of the lamp and not on the edge of its illuminating surface referred to in paragraph 2.10.3.).

In the absence of specific instructions, the lamps constituting a pair shall be symmetrical to one another in relation to the median longitudinal plane, this requirement is not valid with regard to the interior structure of the lamp.
In the absence of specific instructions, the lamps constituting a pair shall satisfy the same colorimetric requirements.
In the absence of specific instructions, the lamps constituting a pair shall have substantially identical photometric characteristics. This shall not apply to a matched pair of a function.
In case of lamps incorporating a manufacturer logo, only two lateral logos (one on each side) or one central logo can be fitted on the rear of the vehicle.
In case of lamps incorporating a manufacturer logo, all logos that are not vehicle manufacturer or body manufacturer logos are prohibited.

On vehicles whose external shape is asymmetrical, the requirements of the preceding paragraphs on the installation of the rear combination lamps (rear position, stop and reversing lamps and retro-reflectors) shall be satisfied so far as is possible.

The rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp and retro-reflector may be grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated with one another provided that all requirements regarding colour, position, orientation, geometric visibility, electrical connections and other requirements, if any, are fulfilled.

The photometric and colorimetric requirements of each lamp of the rear combination lamp shall be fulfilled when all other functions with which this lamp is grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated are switched OFF; however, when the rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with one or more other function(s) which can be switched ON together with it, the requirements regarding colour of each of these other functions shall be fulfilled when the reciprocally incorporated function(s) and the rear position lamp are switched ON.

Where the rear combination lamp contains a single lamp as defined in paragraph 2.14.11.1., subparagraph (a), the apparent surface of which is composed of two or more distinct parts, it shall be installed in such a way that either (a) the total area of the projection of the distinct parts of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis on a plane tangent to the exterior surface of the outer lens and perpendicular to the reference axis occupies not less than 60 per cent of the smallest quadrilateral circumscribing the projection of the said apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis; or (b) the minimum distance between the facing edges of two adjacent/tangential distinct parts of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis does not exceed 75 mm when measured perpendicularly to the reference axis, except that these requirements shall not apply to a single retro-reflector.

Where two or more lamps and/or two or more separate apparent surfaces are included into the same lamp body and/or have a common outer lens, these shall not be considered as an interdependent lamp system.

The maximum height above the ground of each lamp (rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp and retro-reflector) shall be measured from the highest point of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis; where the maximum height above the ground clearly meets the requirements of the Regulation, the exact edges of any surface need not be determined.

The minimum height above the ground of each lamp (rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp and retro-reflector) shall be measured from the lowest point of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis; where the minimum height above the ground clearly meets the requirements of the Regulation, the exact edges of any surface need not be determined.
For the purposes of reducing the geometric visibility angles, the position of a lamp with regard to height above the ground shall be measured from the H plane.

The position of the lamp, as regards width, shall be determined from that edge of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis which is the furthest from the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle when referred to the overall width; where the position, as regards width, clearly meets the requirements of the Regulation, the exact edges of any surface need not be determined.

The position of the lamp, as regards width, shall be determined from the inner edges of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis when referred to the distance between lamps; where the position, as regards width, clearly meets the requirements of the Regulation, the exact edges of any surface need not be determined.

In the absence of specific instructions, the photometric characteristics (e.g. intensity, colour, apparent surface, etc.) of the rear position lamp shall not be intentionally varied during the period when the rear position lamp is switched ON.

In the absence of specific instructions, the photometric characteristics (e.g. intensity, colour, apparent surface, etc.) of the stop lamp shall not be intentionally varied during the period when the stop lamp is switched ON.

In the absence of specific instructions, the photometric characteristics (e.g. intensity, colour, apparent surface, etc.) of the reversing lamp shall not be intentionally varied during the period when the reversing lamp is switched ON.

The photometric characteristics of any lamp of the rear combination lamp may vary in relation to the ambient light, provided that any variation in the photometric characteristics is in compliance with the technical provisions for the lamp concerned.

The photometric characteristics of any lamp of the rear combination lamp may vary as a consequence of other lamps being switched ON or OFF, provided that any variation in the photometric characteristics is in compliance with the technical provisions for the lamp concerned.

The photometric characteristics of any lamp of the rear combination lamp may vary when the lamp is being used to provide another lighting function, provided that any variation in the photometric characteristics is in compliance with the technical provisions for the lamp concerned.

Red light emitted by the rear combination lamp (rear position lamp, stop lamp and retro-reflector) fitted on the rear of the vehicle (as defined in paragraph 2.1.5.) shall not be visible from the front of the vehicle.

For the visibility of red light towards the front of a vehicle, there shall be no direct visibility of the apparent surface of the red rear position lamp, stop lamp or retro-reflector if viewed by an observer moving within Zone 1 in a transverse plane situated 25 m in front of the vehicle (see Annex 4).

In case of doubt, the requirement on the visibility of red light towards the front of the vehicle shall be deemed fulfilled if the luminous intensity of the red light emitted to the front by the rear combination lamp, as verified during type approval of the lamp, is not more than 0.25 cd per lamp taking into account the influence of the vehicle body if applicable.

The electrical connections shall be such that the rear position lamps, together with the front position lamps, the end-outline marker lamps, if they exist, the side-marker lamps, if they exist, and the rear registration plate lamp, can only be switched ON and OFF simultaneously, except while one or more of the following conditions exist: (a) front and rear position lamps, as well as side-marker lamps when combined or reciprocally incorporated with said lamps, are switched ON as parking lamps; (b) side-marker lamps flash in conjunction with direction indicators; (c) daytime running lamps are switched ON; (d) front position lamps function is substituted under the provisions of paragraph 5.12.1.
In the case of an interdependent lamp system, all light sources of the rear position lamp shall be switched ON and OFF simultaneously.
The colour of the light emitted by the reversing lamp shall be white.
The colour of the light emitted by the stop lamp shall be red.
The colour of the light emitted by the rear position lamp shall be red.
The colour of the light reflected by the rear retro-reflector, non-triangular, shall be red.

The number of rear position lamps, stop lamps, reversing lamps and rear retro-reflectors mounted on the vehicle shall be equal to the number indicated in the individual specifications of this Regulation.

Any lamp of the rear combination lamp (rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp, retro-reflector) may be installed on movable components provided that the conditions specified in paragraphs 5.18., 5.19. and 5.20. are fulfilled.

The rear position lamps and rear retro-reflectors may be installed on movable components only if at all fixed positions of the movable components the lamps on the movable components meet all the position, geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements for those lamps.

Where additional rear position lamps or rear retro-reflectors are fitted and are switched ON when the movable component is in any fixed open position, these additional lamps shall satisfy all the position, geometric visibility and photometric requirements applicable to the lamps installed on the movable component.

When the rear combination lamp (rear position, stop and reversing lamps and retro-reflector) is installed on a movable component and the movable component is in the "normal position(s) of use", the lamp shall always return to the position(s) specified by the manufacturer in accordance with this Regulation.

The apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of the rear position lamps shall not be hidden more than 50 per cent by any movable component, with or without a light-signalling device installed on it, in any fixed position different from the "normal position of use", where fixed position of a movable component means the stable or natural rest position(s) of the movable component specified by the vehicle manufacturer, whether locked or not.

The apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of the retro-reflectors shall not be hidden more than 50 per cent by any movable component, with or without a light-signalling device installed on it, in any fixed position different from the "normal position of use", where fixed position of a movable component means the stable or natural rest position(s) of the movable component specified by the vehicle manufacturer, whether locked or not.

If the requirement that the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of the rear position lamps is not hidden more than 50 per cent by any movable component is not practicable, additional lamps satisfying all the position, geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements for the rear position lamps shall be switched ON when the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of these lamps is more than 50 per cent hidden by the movable component.

If the requirement that the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of the retro-reflectors is not hidden more than 50 per cent by any movable component is not practicable, additional devices satisfying all the position, geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements for the retro-reflectors shall be provided for when the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of the retro-reflectors is more than 50 per cent hidden by the movable component.

If the requirement that the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of the rear position lamps is not hidden more than 50 per cent is not practicable and additional lamps are not used, a notice in the vehicle shall inform the user that in certain position(s) of the movable components other road users shall be warned of the presence of the vehicle on the road; for example by means of a warning triangle or other devices according to national requirements for use on the road.

With the exception of retro-reflectors, a lamp of the rear combination lamp (rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp), even bearing an approval mark, is deemed not to be present when it cannot be made to operate by the sole installation of a light source and/or a fuse.

Lamps approved with light source(s) according to UN Regulation No. 37, except when such light sources are used as non-replaceable light source(s) as defined in paragraph 2.9.1.2., shall be fitted in a vehicle in such a way that the light source can be correctly replaced without the need for expert assistance and without the need for special tools, other than those provided with the vehicle by the manufacturer.

For lamps approved with light source(s) according to UN Regulation No. 37, except when such light sources are used as non-replaceable light source(s), the vehicle manufacturer shall provide with the vehicle a detailed description of the procedure for replacement.

In the case where a light source module includes a holder for an approved replaceable light source according to Regulation No. 37, this light source shall be replaceable as required in paragraph 5.23.

Any temporary fail-safe replacement of the light-signalling function of the rear position lamp is allowed, provided that the replacement function in case of a failure is similar in colour, main intensity and position to the function that has ceased to operate and provided that the replacement device remains operational in its original safety function.

During temporary replacement of the light-signalling function of the rear position lamp, a tell-tale on the dashboard (paragraph 2.3.5. of this Regulation) shall indicate occurrence of a temporary replacement and need for repair.

Rear position lamps of category R2 and stop lamps of category S2 with variable luminous intensity control, which respond simultaneously to one or more of the conditions listed in paragraphs 5.26.1. and 5.26.2., are allowed, provided that the intensity of all these lamps, when combined, grouped or reciprocally incorporated, vary all together in the same manner and in a similar proportion.

For rear position lamps of category R2 and stop lamps of category S2 with variable luminous intensity control, in the entire intensity range, the specific prescribed ratio between the luminous intensities of two lamps, if applicable, shall be maintained throughout variation transitions.

Increase and decrease of the luminous intensity of the rear position lamp of category R2 and stop lamp of category S2, in the limits prescribed in the pertinent UN Regulations, is allowed in relation to the following environmental conditions: ambient lighting, fog, snowfall, rain, spray, dust clouds, and contamination of the light emitting surface.

Independent from environmental conditions mentioned under 5.26.1., a decrease of the luminous intensity of the rear position lamp of category R2 and stop lamp of category S2, in the limits prescribed in the pertinent UN Regulations, is allowed as long as the vehicle speed is equal or less than 20 km/h or the distance to the following vehicle is equal or less than 20 m.

As long as the vehicle speed is equal or less than 50 km/h, the intensity decrease of the rear position lamp of category R2 and stop lamp of category S2 already activated under traffic conditions may remain active.
No sharp variation of intensity of the rear position lamp of category R2 and stop lamp of category S2 shall be observed during transition.

When the electrical system of the vehicle is in a constant voltage operating condition, representative for the relevant category of powered vehicle as specified by the applicant, the voltage supplied at the terminals of the rear combination lamp devices which, according to their type approval documentation, have been tested by the application of a special power supply/electronic light source control gear, or in a secondary operating mode or at a voltage requested by the applicant, shall not exceed the voltage specified for the relevant devices or functions as they have been approved, except for devices which include an electronic light source control gear, or a variable intensity control being part of the device, or only light source(s) approved according to UN Regulation No. 128.

In all cases of electric power supply conditions not covered by paragraph 5.27.1., when the electrical system of the vehicle is in a constant voltage operating condition, the voltage at the terminals of the device(s) or function(s) shall not exceed 13.5 V (12 Volt-Systems) by more than 3 per cent, except for devices which include an electronic light source control gear, or a variable intensity control being part of the device, or only light source(s) approved according to UN Regulation No. 128.

In all cases of electric power supply conditions not covered by paragraph 5.27.1., when the electrical system of the vehicle is in a constant voltage operating condition, the voltage at the terminals of the device(s) or function(s) shall not exceed 6.75 V (6 Volt-Systems) by more than 3 per cent, except for devices which include an electronic light source control gear, or a variable intensity control being part of the device, or only light source(s) approved according to UN Regulation No. 128.

In all cases of electric power supply conditions not covered by paragraph 5.27.1., when the electrical system of the vehicle is in a constant voltage operating condition, the voltage at the terminals of the device(s) or function(s) shall not exceed 28 V (24 Volt-Systems) by more than 3 per cent, except for devices which include an electronic light source control gear, or a variable intensity control being part of the device, or only light source(s) approved according to UN Regulation No. 128.
The means of controlling the maximum voltage at the terminals of the rear combination lamp may, for convenience, be located within the body of the device.

There shall be no obstacle on the inside of the angles of geometric visibility to the propagation of light from any part of the apparent surface of the lamp (rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp and retro-reflector) observed from infinity; however, no account is taken of obstacles if they were already presented when the lamp was type-approved.
If measurements of geometric visibility are taken closer to the lamp, the direction of observation shall be shifted parallel to achieve the same accuracy.

If, when the lamp is installed, any part of the apparent surface of the lamp is hidden by any further parts of the vehicle, proof shall be furnished that the part of the lamp not hidden by obstacles still conforms to the photometric values prescribed for the approval of the device.

When the vertical angle of geometric visibility below the horizontal may be reduced to 5° (lamp at less than 750 mm above the ground measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1.), the photometric field of measurements of the installed optical unit may be reduced to 5° below the horizontal.
The LED module of the rear combination lamp (rear position, stop and reversing lamp functions) does not need to be replaceable, if so stated in the communication sheet of the component type approval.

All lamps (devices) of the rear combination lamp (rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp and retro-reflector) shall, where applicable, be type approved according to the corresponding device Regulations as specified in the relevant subparagraphs of paragraph 6 of this Regulation when installed on a vehicle.
In case of light-signalling lamps of the rear combination lamp incorporating a manufacturer logo, the lamp shall be type approved according to the requirements of the UN Regulation No. 148.
The reversing lamp shall be mandatory on motor vehicles.
On motor vehicles of category M1, one reversing lamp device shall be mandatory and a second device shall be optional.

The reversing lamp devices shall be type-approved according to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 23, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.
The reversing lamp shall be positioned in height not less than 250 mm and not more than 1,200 mm above the ground.
The reversing lamp shall be positioned in length at the rear of the vehicle.
The geometric visibility of the reversing lamp installed at the rear of the vehicle shall be defined by angle α = 15° upwards and 5° downwards, as specified in paragraph 2.10.7.

The geometric visibility of the reversing lamp installed at the rear of the vehicle shall be defined by angle β = 45° to right and to left if there is only one device, as specified in paragraph 2.10.7.

The geometric visibility of the reversing lamps installed at the rear of the vehicle shall be defined by angle β = 45° outwards and 30° inwards if there are two devices, as specified in paragraph 2.10.7.
The reversing lamp shall be oriented rearwards.

The electrical connections of the reversing lamp shall be such that the lamp can be switched ON only if the reverse gear is engaged and if the device which controls the starting and stopping of the propulsion system is in such a position that operation of the propulsion system is possible.

The reversing lamp shall not switch ON or remain ON if either the reverse gear is not engaged or the device which controls the starting and stopping of the propulsion system is not in such a position that operation of the propulsion system is possible.
For the reversing lamp, a tell-tale indicating failure is mandatory if required by the component regulation.
Stop lamp devices of S1 or S2 categories shall be mandatory on M1 category vehicles.
The number of S1 or S2 category stop lamp devices shall be two.
The stop lamp devices shall be type-approved according to the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 7, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.

For M1 category vehicles, for S1 or S2 categories stop lamp devices, that point on the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.

S1 or S2 categories stop lamp devices shall be positioned above the ground not less than 350 mm nor more than 1,500 mm (2,100 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 1,500 mm and if the optional lamps are not installed).
S1 or S2 categories stop lamp devices shall be positioned at the rear of the vehicle.

The geometric visibility of S1 or S2 categories stop lamp devices shall have a horizontal angle of 45° to the left and to the right of the longitudinal axis of the vehicle, except that for the stop lamps of categories S1 and S2 mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1.), the inward angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.

The geometric visibility of S1 or S2 categories stop lamp devices shall have a vertical angle of 15° above and below the horizontal, except that where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1.), the downward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.
The orientation of the stop lamp shall be towards the rear of the vehicle.
All stop lamps shall be switched ON simultaneously when the braking system provides the relevant signal defined in UN Regulations Nos. 13 and 13-H.
The stop lamps need not function if the device, which starts and/or stops the propulsion system, is in a position that makes it impossible for the propulsion system to operate.
A tell-tale indicating failure of the stop lamp is mandatory if required by the component regulation.
The installation of rear position lamps of R or R1 or R2 categories shall be mandatory.

The number of rear position lamps shall be two, type-approved according to the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 7, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.
There shall be no special requirement for the arrangement of the rear position lamps.

In width, that point on the apparent surface of the rear position lamp in the direction of the reference axis which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.

In height, the rear position lamp shall be placed above the ground not less than 350 mm nor more than 1,500 mm (2,100 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 1,500 mm and if the optional lamps are not installed).
In length, the rear position lamp shall be positioned at the rear of the vehicle.

The geometric visibility of the rear position lamp shall have a horizontal angle of 45° inwards and 80° outwards, except that where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1.), the inward angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.

The geometric visibility of the rear position lamp shall have a vertical angle of 15° above and below the horizontal, except that where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1.), the downward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.

For M1 category vehicles, as an alternative to paragraph 6.10.5.1., at the discretion of the manufacturer or his duly accredited representative, and only if a rear side-marker lamp is installed on the vehicle, the geometric visibility of the rear position lamp shall have a horizontal angle of 45° outwards to 45° inwards, except that where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1.), the inward angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.

For M1 category vehicles, as an alternative to paragraph 6.10.5.1., at the discretion of the manufacturer or his duly accredited representative, and only if a rear side-marker lamp is installed on the vehicle, the geometric visibility of the rear position lamp shall have a vertical angle of 15° above and below the horizontal, except that where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1.), the downward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.

To be considered visible, the rear position lamp shall provide an unobstructed view of the apparent surface of at least 12.5 square centimetres, the illuminating surface area of any retro-reflector that does not transmit light being excluded.
The orientation of the rear position lamp shall be rearwards.
The electrical connections of the rear position lamp shall be in accordance with paragraph 5.11.
The rear retro-reflector, non-triangular, shall be mandatory on motor vehicles.

The number of rear retro-reflectors, non-triangular, shall be two, type-approved according to the requirements concerning Class IA or IB retro-reflectors in the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 3, or in the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 150.

Additional retro-reflecting devices and materials (including two retro-reflectors not complying with paragraph 6.14.4.) are permitted provided they do not impair the effectiveness of the mandatory lighting and light-signalling devices.

In width, that point on the illuminating surface of the rear retro-reflector which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.

In height, the rear retro-reflector shall be above the ground not less than 250 mm nor more than 900 mm (not more than 1,200 mm if grouped with any rear lamp(s), 1,500 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 900 mm or 1200 mm respectively).
In length, the rear retro-reflector shall be at the rear of the vehicle.
The geometric visibility of the rear retro-reflector shall have a horizontal angle of 30° inwards and outwards.

The geometric visibility of the rear retro-reflector shall have a vertical angle of 10° above and below horizontal, except that where a retro-reflector is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1.), the downward angle of 10° may be reduced to 5°.
The orientation of the rear retro-reflector shall be rearwards.
The illuminating surface of the retro-reflector may have parts in common with the apparent surface of any other lamp situated at the rear.
Any vehicle approved pursuant to this Regulation shall be so manufactured as to conform to the type approved by meeting the requirements set out in paragraphs 5. and 6. above.

For the verification of the visibility of a red lamp to the front (see paragraph 5.10.4. of this Regulation), the zones 1 and 2 explored by the eye of the observer shall be bounded in height by two horizontal planes 1 m and 2.2 m respectively above the ground.

For the verification of the visibility of a red lamp to the front (see paragraph 5.10.4. of this Regulation), the zones 1 and 2 explored by the eye of the observer shall be bounded in width by two vertical planes which, forming to the front and to the rear respectively an angle of 15° outwards from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane, pass through the point or points of contact of vertical planes parallel to the vehicle's median longitudinal plane delimiting the vehicle's overall width; if there are several points of contact, the foremost shall correspond to the forward plane and the rearmost to the rearward plane.

The position of the rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp and retro-reflector, as defined in paragraph 2.1.6. of this Regulation, in width, in height and in length shall be checked in accordance with the general requirements set out in paragraphs 2.10.2., 2.10.3., 2.10.4., 2.3.3. and 5.4. of this Regulation.
The values measured for the distances of the rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp and retro-reflector shall be such that the individual specifications applicable to each lamp are fulfilled.
The angles of geometric visibility of the rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp and retro-reflector shall be checked in accordance with paragraph 2.10.7. of this Regulation.

The values measured for the angles of geometric visibility of the rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp and retro-reflector shall be such that the individual specifications applicable to each lamp are fulfilled except that the limits of the angles may have an allowance corresponding to the ±3º variation permitted in paragraph 5.3. for the mounting of the light-signalling devices.
The visibility of red light from the rear position lamp, stop lamp and retro-reflector towards the front shall be checked in accordance with paragraph 5.10. of this Regulation.
The visibility of white light from the reversing lamp towards the rear shall be checked in accordance with paragraph 5.10. of this Regulation.
The electrical connections of the rear position lamp, stop lamp and reversing lamp shall be checked by switching on every lamp supplied by the electrical system of the vehicle.

The rear position lamp, stop lamp and reversing lamp and their tell-tales shall function in accordance with the provisions set out in paragraphs 5.11. to 5.14. of this Regulation and with the individual specifications applicable to each lamp.

The presence, number, colour, arrangement and, where applicable, the category of the rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp and retro-reflector shall be checked by visual inspection of the lamps and their markings.

The presence, number, colour, arrangement and, where applicable, the category of the rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp and retro-reflector and their markings shall be such that the requirements set out in paragraphs 5.15. and 5.16. as well as in the individual specifications applicable to each lamp are fulfilled.
